subject: Function that works outside of lapply does not work inside

messages.author: 828433663124ca03
messages.subject: Function that works outside of lapply does not work inside
parts:
I have written a function - balk() -   to determine a branch wherein the customer looks at the queue length, and decides to stay (if the queue is short) or to balk (if the queue is long).  When I run the simulation outside of lapply, the function works correctly (people start to balk a lot when the queue is about 5). However when I replicate the same simulation in lapply, no one ever balks and my queue lengths blow up.  It seems that within lapply balk(envs,styNum) isn't returning the correct queue count - but I'm unsure how to correct this - nor do I even understand what is happening.

This is another question basically about how to access info on teh state of the simulation - which is what a majority of my questions have boiled down to so far.  Obviously I'm having issues scaling up from one run to multiple.

Assistance appreciated.  Code below - I included everything that seems relevant.  

balk <- function(envs,styNum) {
        q <- get_queue_count(envs, name = 'stylist')
        p <- sigmoid(q, a = 2, b = styNum) 
        test <- runif(1, min = 0, max = 1)
        if ( test < p) {return(1)} ##Sends the customer to balking
        return(2) ##Sends the customer to a stylist
      
}

t0 <- create_trajectory("Bishops") %>%
        set_attribute("timein", function() now(envs)) %>%
        seize("checkin", 1) %>%
        timeout(function() rtriangle(1, a=.5, b=3,c=1)) %>% 
        release("checkin", 1) %>%
        branch(function() balk(envs,styNum), merge=c(FALSE, TRUE), 
                create_trajectory("balk") %>%
                        set_attribute("balk", function() get_queue_count(envs, name = 'stylist')),
                create_trajectory("style") %>%
                        set_attribute("numCode", function() servCode()) %>%
                        seize("stylist",1) %>%
                        timeout(function() styleTime(numCode)) %>% 
                        release("stylist", 1))

##Define the number of staff
checkNum <- 1
styNum <- 5

##Schedules in case I want to use them
checkSched <- schedule(c(0, 50), c(1,1), period=60)
stySched <- schedule(c(0, 50), c(5,5), period=60)

##Add the resources and the entities
envs %>% 
        add_resource("checkin", checkSched) %>%
        add_resource("stylist", stySched) %>%
        add_generator("customer", t0, function() sched$IAT[(get_n_generated(envs, "customer")) + 1] , mon = 2) 
        #add_generator("customer", t0, function() rexp(1,rate=.2) , mon = 2) 


reps <- 10


envsRep <- lapply(1:reps, function(i) {
        sched <- schedIt() #makes the IATs
        envs <- simmer() 
        
        ##Define the number of staff
        checkNum <- 1
        styNum <- 5
        
        ##Schedules in case I want to use them
        checkSched <- schedule(c(0, 50), c(1,1), period=60)
        stySched <- schedule(c(0, 50), c(5,5), period=60)
        
        ##Add the resources and the entities
        envs %>% 
                add_resource("checkin", checkSched) %>%
                add_resource("stylist", stySched) %>%
                add_generator("customer", t0, function() sched$IAT[(get_n_generated(envs, "customer")) + 1] , mon = 2) 
        
        envs %>% run(until=730)
})

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Function that works outside of lapply does not work inside
parts:
The trajectory, which uses envs, is defined in the global environment, but now your envs is inside a lapply, so the trajectory cannot find it. That is, the same problem as we discussed here, so you have two options:

  • Place the trajectory inside too.
  • Define envs with a double-arrow assignment: envs <<- simmer()
​
